title: chemical
intro:
This component should, for a specific chemical (typically a pesticide), provide a
description of the properties of interest to Daisy.

sections.name: base
sections.desc: Read chemical properties as normal Daisy parameters.

attrs.name: adsorption
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘none’)
        Instant equilibrium between sorbed and solute phases.
        Specify the equilibrium model here for chemicals where the sorbed and solute
        phases typically reaches equilibrium within a single timestep. Slower adsorp-
        tion processes should be modelled as two chemicals, one with ’none’ adsorption
        and one with ’full’ adsorption, and an ’adsorption’ reaction between them.

attrs.name: initial C
attrs.doc:
Optional submodel
    Initial value of the ’C’ parameter. The initial value is given as a sequence of
    (END VALUE) pairs, starting from the top and going down. The parameter
    will be initialized to VALUE from the END of the previous layer, to the END
    of the current layer. Only used if ’C’ is unspecified.
       <     end value    >

attrs.name: – end
attrs.doc: End point of this layer (a negative number).

attrs.name: – value
attrs.doc: Concentration in water.

attrs.name: C
attrs.doc: Concentration in water.

attrs.name: initial
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘initial zero’)
    Initial content (M) if otherwise unspecified. [g/cm3 ].

attrs.name: molar mass
attrs.doc: Molar mass of the chemical.

attrs.name: solubility
attrs.doc: Maximal concentration in water at 20 dg C.

attrs.name: solubility infiltration factor
attrs.doc: Adjustment for maximum concentration in infiltrated water.

attrs.name: crop uptake reflection factor
attrs.doc: How much of the chemical is reflected at crop uptake.

attrs.name: canopy dissipation
attrs.doc: How fast does the chemical dissipate on canopy.

attrs.name: canopy washoff coefficient
attrs.doc: Fraction of the chemical that follows the water off the canopy.

attrs.name: surface decompose
attrs.doc:
Optional component
    How fast does the chemical decompose on surface. Defaults to ’canopy dissipation’
    rate.

attrs.name: litter decompose
attrs.doc:
Optional component
    How fast does the chemical decompose on litter. Default to ’canopy dissipation’
    rate.

attrs.name: litter washoff coefficient
attrs.doc: Fraction of the chemical that follows the water off the litter.

attrs.name: litter diffusion
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘rate’)
        (litter_diffusion rate 0 [h^-1])
        Parameter description:
        How fast chemical diffuse to water passing on surface.

attrs.name: diffusion coefficient
attrs.doc: Diffusion coefficient.

attrs.name: decompose
attrs.doc: How fast the chemical is being decomposed in the soil.

attrs.name: decompose conc factor
attrs.doc: Concentration development factor on decomposition.

attrs.name: decompose lag increment
attrs.doc:
Increment lag with the value of this PLF for the current concentration each
        hour. When lag in any cell reaches 1.0, decomposition begins. It can never
        be more than 1.0 or less than 0.0. By default, there is no lag.

attrs.name: enable surface products
attrs.doc: True if metabolites of this chemical can be generated on the surface.

attrs.name: soil affects surface decompose
attrs.doc: True if soil conditions affect surface decomposition.

attrs.name: drain secondary
attrs.doc:
Concentration in secondary soil water user for drainage. If you set this to
        true the concentration in the secondary domain is used for concentration in
        drain water. Otherwise, the average concentration is the matix is used. Using
        the secondary domain is more physically correct, but also more likely to give
        unstable results.

attrs.name: C below
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘zero gradient’)
        Concentration below the layer of soil being examined. Use a negative number
        to indicate same concentration as in lowest cell.

attrs.name: decompose products
attrs.doc:
Submodel (default: an empty sequence)
        List of products from decomposition.
           <   fraction chemical        >

attrs.name: – fraction
attrs.doc:
Fraction of decomposed matter that become this chemcial.
         If both chemicals have molar mass specified, the fraction will be mole
         based, otherwise it will be mass based.

attrs.name: – chemical
attrs.doc: Chemical product of decomposed matter.

attrs.name: surface storage
attrs.doc:
Stored on the soil surface. This includes the mixing layer, and constitute

attrs.doc: Permanent external source, e.g. subsoil irrigation.

attrs.name: lag
attrs.doc:
This state variable grows with lag increment (C) each hour. When it reached
        1.0, decomposition begins.
Log Variables

attrs.name: spray
attrs.doc: Amount currently being applied.

attrs.name: spray surface
attrs.doc: Amount currently being applied below canopy.

attrs.name: deposit
attrs.doc: Amount deposited from the atmosphere.

attrs.name: spray overhead
attrs.doc: Amount currently being applied above canopy.

attrs.name: surface tillage
attrs.doc: Amount removed from surface due to tillage operations.

attrs.name: litter tillage
attrs.doc: Amount removed from litter due to tillage operations.

attrs.name: snow in
attrs.doc: Entering snow pack.

attrs.name: snow out
attrs.doc: Leaking from snow pack.

attrs.name: canopy in
attrs.doc: Entering canopy.

attrs.name: canopy dissipate
attrs.doc: Dissipating from canopy.

attrs.name: canopy out
attrs.doc: Falling through or off the canopy.

attrs.name: canopy transform
attrs.doc: Added through transformation to canopy.

attrs.name: canopy harvest
attrs.doc: Amount removed with crop harvest.

attrs.name: litter in
attrs.doc: Entering litter .

attrs.name: litter decomposed
attrs.doc: Decomposed from the litter.

attrs.name: litter transform
attrs.doc: Added through transformation in litter layer.

attrs.name: litter out
attrs.doc: Leaking from litter.

attrs.name: litter leak
attrs.doc: Leaking from bottom litter.

attrs.name: litter diffuse
attrs.doc: Diffusing from litter to water passing on surface.

attrs.name: surface solute
attrs.doc: Stored in the soil water of the mixing layer. This is part of ’surface storage’.

attrs.name: surface immobile
attrs.doc: Bound to soil particles in the mixing layer. This is part of ’surface storage’.

attrs.name: surface in
attrs.doc: Falling on the bare soil surface.

attrs.name: surface runoff
attrs.doc: Removed through lateral movement on the soil.

attrs.name: surface decomposed
attrs.doc: Decomposed from the surface.

attrs.name: surface transform
attrs.doc: Added through transformation to surface.

attrs.name: surface mixture
attrs.doc: Entering the soil through mixture with ponded water.

attrs.name: surface out
attrs.doc: Entering the soil with water infiltration.

attrs.name: surface release
attrs.doc:
Fraction of available soil particles released as colloids this timestep. Only
    relevant for chemicals representing colloids.
    The idea behind this is that reactions that generate colloids will set the value of
    this variable, and then reactions that convert immobile chemicals into colloid
    bound chemicals will use it. For this to work, the reactions that set the
    variable must be listed before the reactions that us it.
    Note that the value is relative to the current timestep.

attrs.name: top storage
attrs.doc: Sum of above ground (surface, liter, snow, canopy) storage.

attrs.name: top loss
attrs.doc:
Amount lost from the system from the surface. This includes runoff, canopy
        dissipation and harvest, but not soil infiltration. It also includes the net loss
        through transformation, which can be negative.

attrs.name: C primary
attrs.doc: Concentration in primary domain.

attrs.name: M primary
attrs.doc: Primary domain mass per volume water, soil, and air.

attrs.name: M error
attrs.doc: Mass substracted to avoid negative values.

attrs.name: M tertiary
attrs.doc: Mass in tertiary domain (biopores).

attrs.name: S secondary
attrs.doc: Secondary matrix source term.

attrs.name: S primary
attrs.doc: Primary matrix source term.

attrs.name: S exchange
attrs.doc: Exchange from primary to secondary domain.

attrs.name: S indirect drain
attrs.doc:
Added to the soil matrix from drains indirectly via biopores. This can be
        non-zero whereever there are drain connected biopores.

attrs.name: S soil drain
attrs.doc:
Added to the soil matrix from drains directly, not via biopores. This is only
        non-zero in drain nodes.

attrs.name: S p drain
attrs.doc: Removed from the biopores to the drain. This is only non-zero in drain nodes.

attrs.name: S B2M
attrs.doc: Biopores to matrix.

attrs.name: S M2B
attrs.doc:
Matrix to biopores (negative matrix source). Does not count flow to drain
        connected biopores.

attrs.name: S external
attrs.doc: External source, such as incorporated fertilizer.

attrs.name: S root
attrs.doc: Source term (root uptake only, always negative).

attrs.name: S decompose
attrs.doc: Source term for decompose, is never positive.

attrs.name: S decompose primary
attrs.doc: Source term for decompose in primary domain, is never positive.

attrs.name: S decompose secondary
attrs.doc: Source term for decompose in secondary domain, is never positive.

attrs.name: S transform
attrs.doc: Source term for transformations other than sorption.

attrs.name: decompose factor
attrs.doc: Decompose factor due to soil conditions.

attrs.name: surface decompose factor
attrs.doc: Decompose factor due to soil conditions near surface.

attrs.name: J primary
attrs.doc: Transportation in primary matrix water (positive up).

attrs.name: J secondary
attrs.doc: Transportation in secondary matrix water (positive up).

attrs.name: J matrix
attrs.doc: Transportation in matrix (positive up).

attrs.name: J tertiary
attrs.doc: Transportation in tertiary water (positive up).

attrs.name: tillage
attrs.doc: Changes during tillage.

attrs.name: dt
attrs.doc: Suggested timestep length based on sink terms.

attrs.name: sink cell
attrs.doc: Cell with largest forward sink compared to available matter.

        of (DEPTH VALUE) pairs, starting from the bottom and going up. The
        parameter will be initialized to the the value of the PLF at the center of the
        cell. Only used if ’M’ and ’initial M’ are unspecified.

       M secondary: number [g/cm3 ] soil cells
        Optional state variable
        Secondary domain mass per volume water, soil, and air.

   initial M secondary: submodel (see section 4.1.7) sequence
    Optional submodel
    Initial value of the ’M secondary’ parameter. The initial value is given as a
    sequence of (END VALUE) pairs, starting from the top and going down. The
    parameter will be initialized to VALUE from the END of the previous layer,
    to the END of the current layer. Only used if ’M secondary’ is unspecified.
       <     end value    >
       – end : number [cm]
         Parameter
         End point of this layer (a negative number).
       – value: number [g/cm3 ]
         Parameter
         Secondary domain mass per volume water, soil, and air.
   initial M secondary plf : plf [cm → g/cm3 ]
    Optional parameter
    Initial value of the ’M secondary’ parameter. The initial value is given as a
    sequence of (DEPTH VALUE) pairs, starting from the bottom and going up.
    The parameter will be initialized to the the value of the PLF at the center of
    the cell. Only used if ’M secondary’ and ’initial M secondary’ are unspecified.
   initial M primary: submodel (see section 4.1.7) sequence
    Optional submodel
    Initial value of the ’M primary’ parameter. The initial value is given as a
    sequence of (END VALUE) pairs, starting from the top and going down. The
    parameter will be initialized to VALUE from the END of the previous layer,
    to the END of the current layer. Only used if ’M primary’ is unspecified.
       <     end value    >
       – end : number [cm]
         Parameter
         End point of this layer (a negative number).
       – value: number [g/cm3 ]
         Parameter
         Primary domain mass per volume water, soil, and air.
   initial M primary plf : plf [cm → g/cm3 ]
    Optional parameter
    Initial value of the ’M primary’ parameter. The initial value is given as a
    sequence of (DEPTH VALUE) pairs, starting from the bottom and going up.
    The parameter will be initialized to the the value of the PLF at the center of
    the cell. Only used if ’M primary’ and ’initial M primary’ are unspecified.
   Ms: number [<fraction>] soil cells
    Optional parameter
    Mass in dry soil. This include all matter in both soil and water, relative to
    the dry matter weight. Only for initialization of the ’M’ parameter.
   initial Ms: submodel (see section 4.1.7) sequence
    Optional submodel
    Initial value of the ’Ms’ parameter. The initial value is given as a sequence of
    (END VALUE) pairs, starting from the top and going down. The parameter
    will be initialized to VALUE from the END of the previous layer, to the END
    of the current layer. Only used if ’Ms’ is unspecified.
       <     end value    >

          – end : number [cm]
            Parameter
            End point of this layer (a negative number).
          – value: number [<fraction>]
            Parameter
            Mass in dry soil. This include all matter in both soil and water, relative
            to the dry matter weight. Only for initialization of the ’M’ parameter.

       initial Ms plf : plf [cm → <fraction>]
        Optional parameter
        Initial value of the ’Ms’ parameter. The initial value is given as a sequence
        of (DEPTH VALUE) pairs, starting from the bottom and going up. The
        parameter will be initialized to the the value of the PLF at the center of the
        cell. Only used if ’Ms’ and ’initial Ms’ are unspecified.

       S permanent: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        State variable (default: an empty sequence)
        Permanent external source, e.g. subsoil irrigation.

       lag: number (dimensionless) soil cells
        Optional state variable
        This state variable grows with lag increment (C) each hour. When it reached
        1.0, decomposition begins.

Log Variables
       spray: number [g/m2 /h]
        Amount currently being applied.

       spray surface: number [g/m2 /h]
        Amount currently being applied below canopy.

       deposit: number [g/m2 /h]
        Amount deposited from the atmosphere.

       spray overhead : number [g/m2 /h]
        Amount currently being applied above canopy.

       surface tillage: number [g/m2 /h]
        Amount removed from surface due to tillage operations.

       litter tillage: number [g/m2 /h]
        Amount removed from litter due to tillage operations.

       snow in: number [g/m2 /h]
        Entering snow pack.

       snow out: number [g/m2 /h]
        Leaking from snow pack.

       canopy in: number [g/m2 /h]
        Entering canopy.

       canopy dissipate: number [g/m2 /h]
        Dissipating from canopy.

       canopy out: number [g/m2 /h]
        Falling through or off the canopy.

   canopy transform: number [g/m2 /h]
    Added through transformation to canopy.
   canopy harvest: number [g/m2 /h]
    Amount removed with crop harvest.
   litter in: number [g/m2 /h]
    Entering litter .
   litter decomposed : number [g/m2 /h]
    Decomposed from the litter.
   litter transform: number [g/m2 /h]
    Added through transformation in litter layer.
   litter out: number [g/m2 /h]
    Leaking from litter.

   litter leak : number [g/m2 /h]
    Leaking from bottom litter.
   litter diffuse: number [g/m2 /h]
    Diffusing from litter to water passing on surface.

   surface solute: number [g/m2 ]
    Stored in the soil water of the mixing layer. This is part of ’surface storage’.
   surface immobile: number [g/m2 ]
    Bound to soil particles in the mixing layer. This is part of ’surface storage’.

   surface in: number [g/m2 /h]
    Falling on the bare soil surface.
   surface runoff : number [g/m2 /h]
    Removed through lateral movement on the soil.
   surface decomposed : number [g/m2 /h]
    Decomposed from the surface.
   surface transform: number [g/m2 /h]
    Added through transformation to surface.
   surface mixture: number [g/m2 /h]
    Entering the soil through mixture with ponded water.

   surface out: number [g/m2 /h]
    Entering the soil with water infiltration.
   surface release: number [<fraction>]
    Fraction of available soil particles released as colloids this timestep. Only
    relevant for chemicals representing colloids.
    The idea behind this is that reactions that generate colloids will set the value of
    this variable, and then reactions that convert immobile chemicals into colloid
    bound chemicals will use it. For this to work, the reactions that set the
    variable must be listed before the reactions that us it.
    Note that the value is relative to the current timestep.
   top storage: number [g/m2 ]
    Sum of above ground (surface, liter, snow, canopy) storage.

       top loss: number [g/m2 /h]
        Amount lost from the system from the surface. This includes runoff, canopy
        dissipation and harvest, but not soil infiltration. It also includes the net loss
        through transformation, which can be negative.

       C primary: number [g/cm3 ] soil cells
        Concentration in primary domain.

       M primary: number [g/cm3 ] soil cells
        Primary domain mass per volume water, soil, and air.

       M error : number [g/cm3 ] soil cells
        Mass substracted to avoid negative values.

       M tertiary: number [g/cm3 ] soil cells
        Mass in tertiary domain (biopores).

       S secondary: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Secondary matrix source term.

       S primary: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Primary matrix source term.

       S exchange: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Exchange from primary to secondary domain.

       S indirect drain: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Added to the soil matrix from drains indirectly via biopores. This can be
        non-zero whereever there are drain connected biopores.

       S soil drain: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Added to the soil matrix from drains directly, not via biopores. This is only
        non-zero in drain nodes.

       S p drain: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Removed from the biopores to the drain. This is only non-zero in drain nodes.

       S B2M : number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Biopores to matrix.

       S M2B : number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Matrix to biopores (negative matrix source). Does not count flow to drain
        connected biopores.

       S external : number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        External source, such as incorporated fertilizer.

       S root: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Source term (root uptake only, always negative).

       S decompose: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Source term for decompose, is never positive.

       S decompose primary: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Source term for decompose in primary domain, is never positive.

       S decompose secondary: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Source term for decompose in secondary domain, is never positive.

    S transform: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
     Source term for transformations other than sorption.

    decompose factor : number (dimensionless) soil cells
     Decompose factor due to soil conditions.

    surface decompose factor : number (dimensionless)
     Decompose factor due to soil conditions near surface.

    J primary: number [g/cm2 /h] soil edges
     Transportation in primary matrix water (positive up).

    J secondary: number [g/cm2 /h] soil edges
     Transportation in secondary matrix water (positive up).

    J matrix : number [g/cm2 /h] soil edges
     Transportation in matrix (positive up).

    J tertiary: number [g/cm2 /h] soil edges
     Transportation in tertiary water (positive up).

    tillage: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
     Changes during tillage.

    dt: number [h]
     Suggested timestep length based on sink terms.

    sink cell : integer
     Cell with largest forward sink compared to available matter.

sections.name: FOCUS
sections.desc:
A ‘base’ model (see 23.1, page 125) build into Daisy.
   Pesticides inspired by FOCUS surface water.
   Depth, moisture, and heat effect according to the FOCUS Surface Water WG.
    Water factor is zero below 0.5 Theta wp, one above field capacity, and ((Theta
- 0.5 Theta wp) / (Theta fc - 0.5 Theta wp))B otherwise. From MACRO 5.2.
   Heat factor is zero below zero degrees, 0.2 T eˆ(alpha (5 - T ref)) below 5 dg C,
and and eˆ(alpha (T - T ref)) above 5 dg C. From MACRO 5.0.
   Depth factor is specified by ’z’ and ’z factor’. See also [FOCUS, 2002, FOCUS, 2012]

     will be scaled so it is 1 at this temperature..

attrs.name: decompose SMB pool
attrs.doc:
SMB pool for Michaelis-Menten kinetics. Use 0 for SMB1, 1 for SMB2, or -1
     for all SMB pools.

attrs.name: decompose SMB KM
attrs.doc:
Michaelis-Menten kinetics parameter. Decompose rate is modified by C /
     (KM + C), where C is the carbon content in the pool specified by ’decom-
     pose SMB pool’.

attrs.name: SMB ref
attrs.doc:
Reference SMB carbon for docomposition of mulch. The SMB factor for
     decomposition will be scaled so it is 1 at this amount of SMB carbon. By
     default, it will not be scaled.

              (initial C secondary plf initial C secondary plf )
              (initial C primary initial C primary ...)
              (initial C primary plf initial C primary plf )
              (M M ...)
              (initial M initial M ...)
              (initial M plf initial M plf )

              (lag lag ...) >

    T ref : number [dg C]
     Parameter (default 10)
     Reference temperature for decomposition. The heat factor on decomposition
     will be scaled so it is 1 at this temperature..

    decompose heat factor : plf [dg C → <none>]
     Parameter (has default value with 0 points)
     Heat factor on decomposition.

    decompose water factor : plf [cm → <none>]
     Parameter (has default value with 0 points)
     Water potential factor on decomposition.

    decompose SMB pool : integer
     Parameter (default 1)
     SMB pool for Michaelis-Menten kinetics. Use 0 for SMB1, 1 for SMB2, or -1
     for all SMB pools.

    decompose SMB KM : number [g C/cm3 ]
     Parameter (default 0)
     Michaelis-Menten kinetics parameter. Decompose rate is modified by C /
     (KM + C), where C is the carbon content in the pool specified by ’decom-
     pose SMB pool’.

    SMB ref : number [g C/cm3 ]
     Optional parameter
     Reference SMB carbon for docomposition of mulch. The SMB factor for
     decomposition will be scaled so it is 1 at this amount of SMB carbon. By
     default, it will not be scaled.

    decompose CO2 factor : plf [g CO2-C/cm3 /h → <none>]
     Parameter (has default value with 0 points)
     CO2 development factor on decomposition.

    decompose depth factor : plf [cm → <none>]
     Parameter (has default const value 1 [])
     Depth influence on decomposition.
